decisive_spans.text: A woman in her 60s presented with multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva. The lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased to approximately 60 lesions
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules present on the central face and around the eyes, with similar papules noted on the vulva
Eight lesions underwent biopsy, showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces. Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples    - Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples

response.rationale: The patient presents with multiple lesions, a family history of similar lesions, and histopathological features consistent with infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma, along with a SUFU gene mutation. D8, Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas, encompasses all these findings. D4, Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma, describes the specific type of carcinoma but does not fully capture the multiplicity and hereditary aspect. D2, Generalized Basaloid Follicular Hamartoma Syndrome, is less specific and doesn't account for the confirmed carcinoma. D1, Meningioma, is a co-occurring condition but not the primary diagnosis for the skin lesions. D6, Basal Cell Carcinoma, is too general.
